model: Series RHPX humidity/temperature communicating transmitter, BACnet MS/TP
applies_to: Dwyer Series RHPX duct, space and outdoor humidity/temperature transmitters with the BACnet MS/TP / Modbus RTU communication option.
summary: The RHPX Comms reports relative humidity and temperature plus calculated dew point, enthalpy and absolute humidity over BACnet MS/TP or Modbus RTU. On BACnet each calculated value is a separate Analog Input per unit system; two Analog Values hold the humidity and temperature offsets and two Multi-State Values set what the display shows.
notes: Each derived value is given twice, in metric and imperial units, as separate objects.
The guide also lists a Network Port object (NP1, "MS/TP"); it is not repeated here.
The overview table prints AI 6 as "Absolute Humidity g/m3"; the property table name "Absolute Humidity g/m^3" is used here.
AI 7 uses a vendor-specific units code (532) for lb per million cubic feet.
MV 2 state texts are printed with "Due Point" (sic).

source.title: Series RHPX Humidity/Temperature Communicating Transmitter - User's Guide

integration.summary: Set the address with the DIP switches, select BACnet MS/TP, and read AI 1 humidity and AI 8 or AI 9 temperature; dew point, enthalpy and absolute humidity are ready-made if the BMS needs them.
setup: Ships set for Modbus RTU at address 127; a DIP switch selects BACnet MS/TP.
Device instance defaults to 607xxx, where xxx is the address set on the DIP switches.
MS/TP at 9600 to 115200 baud, 8 data bits; Max Master defaults to 127 and Max Info Frames to 1.
DeviceCommunicationControl and ReinitializeDevice need the password "Dwyer".
gotchas: Offsets (AV 1, AV 2) are limited to ±3.5 %RH and ±5 °F.

points.name: Absolute Humidity lb/MMCF
points.description: Absolute humidity, lb per million cubic feet

points.name: Humidity Display Measurement
points.states: 1=Due Point (degrees F), 2=Due Point (degrees C), 3=Relative Humidity (%RH), 4=Enthalpy (BTU/lb), 5=Absolute Humidity (lb/MMCF), 6=Enthalpy (kJ/kg), 7=Absolute Humidity (g/m^3)
